# English candidate admission fixtures

Authored positive and negative cases for KBD-A13. The development split includes the reported `xin` noise and existing English acceptance. Validation uses distinct inputs and was frozen before native execution; it exposed policy gaps and is now regression material. The file named `holdout.tsv` was originally frozen after those fixes; all splits have now been inspected and are regression material. There are 20 development and 17 regression-validation inputs, for 49 inputs and 98 input/page-size combinations. The small authored set does not estimate general user accuracy.

TSV fields: case ID, raw ASCII input, required first-page candidate (`-` for none), maximum ASCII-word candidates, Chinese-first flag. Each case runs on both five- and nine-candidate native menus. Positive cases require actual engine selection and one commit; negative cases cancel without insertion. `provenance.json` pins the current fixture bytes. Updated expectations cover bounded English display, deferred short prefixes and normal-Pinyin homographs. An early-exhausted Chinese stream (`engin`) may naturally leave more room for English. Unknown source frequency does not mean an invalid English word.

Reproduce on macOS with `node scripts/test-keyboard-input.mjs --report /tmp/arion-admission-run/report.json`; on an ordinary Windows desktop use `node scripts/test-windows-pinyin.mjs` after staging its runtime. These commands use isolated synthetic profiles. Actual installed IMK/TSF dispatch remains separate.
